title: Five-month-olds in one study still reasoned about a hidden object after several minutes
summary: Luo, Baillargeon, Brueckner, and Munakata reported that five-month-olds reasoned about a hidden object after the objects were never shown together and a delay of three or four minutes.
body: A 2003 paper in Cognition by Luo, Baillargeon, Brueckner, and Munakata tested two rival readings of earlier looking-time work. Five-month-old infants succeeded at reasoning about a visible object together with a hidden one even though the two were never visible at the same time, and even though three or four minutes passed before the test trials. The authors present that success as evidence for robust representations of hidden objects in these infants. This card states their report. It does not repeat the trials.

sources.title: Reasoning about a hidden object after a delay: evidence for robust representations in 5-month-old infants
sources.author: Yuyan Luo, Renée Baillargeon, Laura Brueckner, and Yuko Munakata
sources.note: Supports the abstract's result: success when the objects were never simultaneously visible and a 3- or 4-minute delay preceded the test. Cognition 2003;88(3):B23-B32.
